objective: Test whether known one-large-cofactor pairing reduces charged separator construction on heldout synthetic semiprimes, compared with smooth-only and established SIQS. No new algorithm or RSA-270 extrapolation.
generation: p from sha256(PREFIX:label:p); q from first sha256(PREFIX:label:q{i}), i=0..63, with |p-q|>2^(bits_each_prime-6); low bits + binary 11 + odd, then sympy nextprime; n=pq; factor hashes stored without exposing factors to solver

comparator_arms.A: streamed smooth-only relations plus GF2 dependence
comparator_arms.B: A plus paired equal residual cofactor up to declared limit and exact square witness
comparator_arms.C: SymPy 1.14 SIQS, same n and explicitly charged total execution, recognized prior-art strong baseline
comparator_arms.D: bounded Fermat and Pollard rho traditional controls

primary_metric: number of candidate x^2-n values fully trial-divided before independently verified nontrivial congruence-of-squares gcd; failed arms right-censored at 60000
secondary_metrics: wall-clock with overhead, separately per arm
strong comparator successful counts and speed
success_condition: B strictly beats A on heldout median factor-witness candidate cost and does not reduce successes; any scientific advantage additionally requires B outperform an actually executed full-information mature comparator in total cost and a novel operation beyond published single-large-prime methods
hard_limits: No genuine blindness claim (synthetic), no new factoring law from known one-large-prime variant, preserve negative controls and independently unqualified results as UNKNOWN.
